measurement.mode: headless CPU loading and scene-lifecycle verification
measurement.environment_note: PERF_LOG=1 was set explicitly; all other environment variables were inherited. No DISPLAY or FPS override was set.
measurement.command_provenance: Exact executable, arguments and explicit environment supplied by the benchmark runner; SWITCH_START records independently report mode, engine and route.
measurement.sampling_note: Four serial runs with one observation per load. These are measured samples, not confidence intervals or target-hardware FPS.
measurement.ready_s_definition: Wall time from initial scene load or Tab input until a replacement Game, correct mounted region, active camera, populated navigation, and supported player are ready; excludes the subsequent eight settling frames and movement check.
measurement.phase_definition: LOAD_PHASE timings are milliseconds. nav.total includes nav.bake/nav.stitch where applicable; totals must not be added to their components. Null means no phase record was emitted, as on a cache hit that skips baking.

cache_state_definitions.baked: Conditioned region scene cache was generated in this load.
cache_state_definitions.miss_rebuilt: Navigation cache lookup missed and a bake occurred.
cache_state_definitions.not_implemented_recomputed: Stitch metadata reuse was not implemented at this stage.
cache_state_definitions.bypassed_recomputed: --no-stitch-cache forced the original link search; computed metadata could still be persisted.

measurement.scope: headless_runs; rendered runs have separate mode and settings below

interpretation: rebuild_nav first visits to town/desert generated conditioned-region caches. These are first observed cache misses, not controlled cold filesystem-cache measurements.
cached_nav reused the conditioned regions and baked navigation, but still recomputed stitch links on every visit.

The final nav_world implementation changed the script stamp in the navigation key. uncached_stitch therefore rebaked town and desert on their first visits, despite region-cache hits. Its return to town hit the now-current baked-navigation cache.
The controlled stitch comparison uses only the return-to-town load in uncached_stitch versus cached_stitch: both region and baked-navigation caches hit, on the same implementation and route.
The desert change from 9.409387 to 2.024023 seconds includes skipping a 6737.399 ms Recast bake as well as stitch reuse. It is not a stitch-only improvement.
Headless mode does not validate OpenGL rendering or GPU performance. Rendered/software-renderer results are recorded separately.

Passing local movement verifies the tested spawn routes; unchanged navigation warnings and unreached groups remain visible in diagnostics. It does not prove every authored navigation edge is traversable.

controlled_warm_town_comparison.cache_control: Both observations hit conditioned-region and baked-navigation caches. --no-stitch-cache is the only invocation difference. OS cache and ordinary timing noise were not controlled.

failure_analysis.classification: movement harness wall-clock timing limitation under software rendering
failure_analysis.interpretation: The wetlands replacement had a valid camera, navigation and supported player at SWITCH_READY, but the required one-metre movement was not verified before the old eight-wall-second movement deadline. This run is a failure, not a completed full cycle.
failure_analysis.causal_note: At roughly two achieved physics ticks per wall second with a four-step-per-frame cap, eight wall seconds provide only a fraction of a simulated second. The log records actual movement, but not the required distance.
failure_analysis.followup: The harness was changed to allow eight seconds of physics ticks while keeping the per-stage wall timeout and unchanged distance/support assertions. Production game code was unchanged by this harness adjustment; the rerun is recorded separately only after completion.

rendered_measurement.mode: Compatibility OpenGL, X11 window, software rendering
rendered_measurement.interpretation: These rendered runs test native-crash behavior, visible rendering, replacement readiness and movement. Software rendering is not a measurement of the user GPU; different cache states mean the timings are not a controlled performance comparison.
rendered_measurement.completion_rule: Only runs ending in SWITCH_PASS, SWITCH_FAIL, or a recorded native crash are included. A requested full cycle is not counted as completed after an early crash or movement assertion failure.

renderer_diagnosis.summary: Regenerating main-mesh LODs while retaining the imported optimized shadow mesh creates incompatible LOD index ranges. GLES3 selects an LOD from the main surface and applies that same index to the shadow surface.
renderer_diagnosis.repair: Clear shadow_mesh only on meshes whose main LODs were regenerated. The existing renderer fallback uses the main surface for shadows, so both passes use matching LOD buffers. Ordinary shadows remain enabled; skipped and unmodified meshes retain compatible source shadows.

fault_attribution.interpretation: Instruction pattern matches one-based LOD index minus one, 16-byte Surface::LOD stride, and 12-byte index_buffer member offset. This is source/disassembly attribution of an inlined operation, not full debug-symbol symbolization.
fault_attribution.source_correspondence: The exact 4.6.3 GLES3 source selects the main-surface LOD, uses the shadow surface during shadow rendering, and indexes that surface with the chosen LOD. The fault instruction and surrounding index arithmetic match this inlined buffer access. This is source/disassembly attribution, not a named stack trace from debug symbols.

renderer_diagnosis.runtime_api_probe: ImporterMesh.has_method("create_shadow_mesh") returned false on exact Godot 4.6.3; regenerating an optimized shadow mesh through this internal API is unavailable to GDScript.

final_unit_regressions.scope: Five small regression suites passed on both Godot 4.6.3 and 4.7.2; no whole-map performance work is done by these fixtures.

water_cache_parity.problem: Cold conditioning finalized the gameplay waterline, but a warm cache load remeasured the modified visual meshes. Wetlands could change from 0.000 m on first load to 0.050 m on a cache hit, changing gameplay water state and the navigation cache key.
water_cache_parity.repair: Save and restore finalized water presence, level and footprint cells with the conditioned region, together with the generated water extension and barrier. Invalid or legacy metadata triggers reconditioning instead of reuse of inconsistent state.
fixture_coverage: Real conditioned-region save/load branches for wet and dry synthetic geometry.
Finalized level and every footprint cell retained; cold/warm navigation keys match.
Generated extension/barrier geometry, world transforms, ownership and shadow settings preserved without duplicate regeneration.
Invalid or missing metadata cannot partially alter state; legacy/corrupt region caches rebuild and are reusable afterward.
water_cache_parity.full_map_validation_note: Final map-cycle verification is recorded separately from earlier measurements and renderer runs that preceded this parity change.

full_map_validation.result: Both wetlands visits preserve gameplay level 0.000 m and 11445 nav polygons. Every map in the second cycle hits region/nav/stitch caches without rebaking.

final_rendered_validation.result: Wetlands retains cached and gameplay water level 0.000 m and 11445 navigation polygons on the final rendered full cycle.

final_headless_runs.movement_budget: 8 simulated seconds (480 physics ticks at 60 Hz), with a 300-second per-stage wall limit
final_headless_runs.interpretation: Ten verified transitions on the final production code. The first visit to each region regenerates its conditioned-region cache after the water-state change; navigation cache availability is recorded per load. The second cycle reuses all three cache layers and performs no navigation bake. These headless observations are independent of the earlier controlled town comparison and are not rendered FPS measurements.
